meta.scope: U.S. Air Force MQ-9 / MQ-9A Reaper (Active force + Air National Guard). Holdings of other services and foreign operators are not included.
notes: The headline figure is the most recent officially-stated fleet total, NOT a sum of the loss events below.

Loss events are documented individually for context. Yemen tallies in particular overlap between Houthi claims and U.S. acknowledgements, so events should not be added together to derive the fleet size.

totals.label: Sep 2024
totals.note: Air Force-stated total as of September 2024.

source.title: How big is the Air Force's Reaper drone fleet?

totals.label: End FY2025
totals.note: 158 Active force + 24 Air National Guard, per congressional testimony (Lt. Gen. David Tabor).

source.title: To Replace Lost MQ-9s, USAF Eyes Next-Gen Reaper

totals.label: May 2026
totals.note: Fleet total after Operation Epic Fury losses, per Lt. Gen. Tabor's May 20, 2026 testimony — roughly 54 aircraft below the service's 189-aircraft floor.

source.title: Air Force dubs MQ-9 the 'MVP' of Epic Fury as lawmakers press manned-unmanned future

events.title: 24 MQ-9s lost in Operation Epic Fury (U.S.-Iran war)
events.summary: A Congressional Research Service report states the U.S. lost 24 MQ-9 Reapers during the 2026 war with Iran — most shot down by air defenses, some destroyed on the ground at regional bases. Roughly 20% of the fleet.

sources.title: 42 aircraft lost or damaged in Operation Epic Fury, congressional report says
Air Force Chief: MQ-9 Reaper 'Most Valuable Player' of Iran War Despite Losses

events.title: MQ-9 crashes into the Yellow Sea off South Korea
events.summary: An MQ-9 of the 431st Expeditionary Reconnaissance Squadron (Kunsan AB) went down in the Yellow Sea during a routine mission. It was later recovered by U.S. and ROK forces.

sources.title: Air Force recovers Reaper drone that crashed last month off South Korea

events.title: ~7 MQ-9s lost over Yemen, spring 2025 campaign
events.summary: A U.S. official confirmed at least seven MQ-9s were lost in the Yemen area since mid-March 2025 during intensified operations against the Houthis. This is an aggregate count, not a single incident.

sources.title: US has lost 7 multi-million-dollar drones in Yemen area since March — official

events.title: MQ-9 claimed downed over Marib
events.summary: The Houthis claimed downing an MQ-9 over Marib governorate, their first MQ-9 claim of 2025.

sources.title: How the Houthis' strikes on US MQ-9 Reaper drones serve a wider regional agenda

events.title: MQ-9 ditched in the Mediterranean after propeller loss
events.summary: A 432nd Wing MQ-9 lost its propeller mid-flight (a gearbox spiral lock ring failure) and was intentionally ditched in the Mediterranean Sea. An Accident Investigation Board put the loss at about $13 million.

sources.title: Broken propeller caused $13M military Reaper drone to crash into sea

events.title: MQ-9 claimed downed over Al Bayda
events.summary: Houthi spokesman Yahya Sare'e announced the downing of an MQ-9 over Al Bayda governorate.

sources.title: How the Houthis' strikes on US MQ-9 Reaper drones serve a wider regional agenda

events.title: Two MQ-9s downed over Yemen, September 2024
events.summary: The U.S. military acknowledged that the Houthis shot down two MQ-9s in September 2024, including one reportedly downed over Dhamar province.

sources.title: Houthi rebels claim they shot down another US MQ-9 Reaper drone

events.title: MQ-9 downed near Hodeida
events.summary: An MQ-9 was shot down near the Red Sea port of Al Hudaydah, an early loss in the Houthi campaign against U.S. drones.

sources.title: Houthi rebels say US-made drone shot down over Yemen
